Theme

injure verb

hurt a person or an animal

also injured, be injured, get hurt, injury, wounded

classical

Caes. BG 5.35 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sest. 24 (Lewis & Short)

vulnerō, vulnerāre, vulnerāvī, vulnerātum

verb, first conjugation

wound, injure

To wound, by a blow, a weapon or a fall; the wound is vulnus (see wound). With the part hurt in the accusative: volnerātus umerum (Plin. NH 7.103, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • laedō, laedere, laesī, laesum — hurt, injure, damage

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short: “to hurt by striking, wound, injure, damage”

    The general word for harm done to a body or a thing (see damage), and to feelings. For hurting oneself, mihi nocuī (see hurt yourself).

  • sauciō, sauciāre, sauciāvī, sauciātum — wound, hurt

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.1.67: Rubrius in turbā sauciātur (Lewis & Short)

    Class. but rare, not in Caesar (Lewis & Short); the adjective saucius, wounded, is common.

Examples

  • L. Cotta lēgātus in adversum ōs fundā vulnerātur

    the legate Lucius Cotta is struck full in the face by a sling-stoneCaes. BG 5.35 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nēmō vulnerātus est.

    No one was hurt.composed

See also wound, hurt yourself, hurt, damage, bruise.
